commitResults.messageTitle: Show all homework after deleting overdue homework
commitResults.messageBody:
After a homework delete, the result lists only the student's upcoming
homework with its new numbers. When the deleted record was due before
today, the other overdue records are renumbered but not shown, so a
second delete typed from the earlier `hw ls N all` list can remove a
different record than the tutor meant, with no undo.

Let's list all of the student's homework, as `hw ls N all` does, when
the deleted record was due before today. Deleting upcoming homework
keeps the shorter upcoming list.

Update the UG and DG to describe the list shown.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report the student index first in homework list
commitResults.messageBody:
`hw ls all 1` says "The word after STUDENT_INDEX can only be all, but
found 1.", although the user's mistake is the word order: `all` was
typed where the student index goes. `hw ls all` already reports the
index for the same first word.

Let's check the syntax of the first word before checking the word
after it, so `hw ls all 1` reports the student index, as `hw ls all`
does. `hw ls 1 2` still names the second word.

commitResults.messageTitle: Point subject/ after a title to s/
commitResults.messageBody:
`hw add 1 title/Essay subject/MATH due/2026-12-01` answers "subject/
is not a prefix of this command. If subject/ is part of the title, put
the whole title in straight double quotes". A user who knows `title/`
as the long form of `t/` may guess `subject/` for `s/`, and the hint
tells them to quote a title that is already right.

Let's give `subject/` after a title the hint "Use s/ for the subject."
instead of the quote hint, in `homework add` and `homework edit`.
`subject/` is still not accepted, so there is one subject prefix to
learn. Elsewhere `subject/` keeps the plain unknown-prefix error, which
is not misleading.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report an invalid index first in hw edit and marks
commitResults.messageBody:
`hw e 0 2` answers "Specify at least one field to edit" and `hw m 0 1`
answers "Missing required prefix(es): score/", although the student
index 0 is also wrong. The user fixes the named problem and then gets
the index error, while `hw e 0 2 t/X` names the index at once.

Let's check the syntax of both indices before checking for a field to
edit or for `score/`, and update the documented check order. A prefix
glued to the homework index, as in `hw m 1 2score/5`, is now reported
as an invalid homework index, which is where the typing slip is.

commitResults.messageTitle: Read data file keys in any case
commitResults.messageBody:
A hand-edited key in another case, such as "Score" or "Status", is
ignored when the data file loads, and the next save removes it, so
the scores and statuses typed by hand are lost without any warning.

Let's read keys in any case, so "Score" is read as "score" and saved
back as "score". A key repeated in another case, such as "score" and
"Score" in one homework, is rejected as a repeated key: Jackson
accepts it and keeps only one value, which would lose the other one
silently, so the file is checked again after reading it, comparing
keys in lower case.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject data file keys that TutorFlow does not use
commitResults.messageBody:
A key in the data file that no adapter uses, such as "homework" typed
for "homeworks", is ignored when the file loads, and the next save
removes it. A typo made while hand-editing therefore deletes a whole
homework list, its scores and statuses, without any message.

Let's reject such a key when the data file loads, as every other
invalid hand edit is rejected: the file is not loaded and not changed,
and the reason names the key and its line and column, e.g.

  The key "homework" near line 9, column 5 is not a key TutorFlow
  uses. Check its spelling.

Jackson reports an unknown key only at the end of its object, so the
key's own position is found by following the path Jackson gives to
it. The check applies to the data file only (students, homework,
lessons and the top level); preferences.json still ignores keys it
does not use, as in AB3, so a stray key there cannot reset the
window settings.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add homework delete steps to DG manual testing
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG manual tests for deleting homework give an exact result only
for a successful delete; the error cases say just "an error message",
and nothing checks the renumbering of homework due before today.

Let's give the exact messages for `homework delete 1 0`, `hw del 3 2`,
`hw del 5 1` and `hw del 1`, and add steps that delete two overdue
records in a row using the numbers shown after the first delete. The
outputs are copied from the JAR.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the student list reset to DG use case UC05
commitResults.messageBody:
UC05 says only that `homework upcoming` displays the due homework.
The command also shows all students again in roster order, clearing
any search, filter or sort, so that the student index of each record
matches the student list, but the use case leaves this out.

Let's add it as its own step and renumber the extensions after it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain typing an earlier date this year in UG
commitResults.messageBody:
A due date typed as `MM-DD` that has already passed this year means
next year. A tutor who corrects an overdue record with `hw e 1 3
due/10-25` on 1 November gets 2027-10-25, and the record moves out of
the overdue count. The UG states the year rule but not what to type
instead.

Let's tell the user, in `homework add` and `homework edit`, to type the
full YYYY-MM-DD date for a date earlier this year.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the edit and marks result layout in UG
commitResults.messageBody:
`hw e` and `hw m` show the changed record as "Ethan Lim (91234567);
Title: ...; Subject: ...; Due: ...", without its number or status,
while add, list and delete use the numbered `homework list` layout.
The UG does not say so, so the difference looks like a bug.

Let's say in `homework edit` and `homework marks` which details the
result shows and where to see the rest. The layouts stay as they are,
as agreed in Issue #134.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #210 from Elljaykei/jk-week12-release-cleanup
commitResults.messageBody:
Finalize JK code and documentation for v1.6

Fix the remaining issues found in the final audit of the homework
and lesson features before the v1.6 release:

* homework filter prints indices in ASCII digits in every locale, so
  they can be typed back into later commands
* equal homework filter and status commands now have equal hash codes
* the lesson edit diagram calls buildSchedule, matching the code

Also expand single-line Javadoc comments to the course format, set
the version label to V1.6, declare the AI assistance used in the
Developer Guide, and make the section-scrolling test wait until the
result text really overflows.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #207 from Alexc09/206-beta-homework-fixes
commitResults.messageBody:
Fix beta-test bugs in homework and saving

Fix the homework and saving bugs found in the beta round, so users see
the right records and do not lose hand-edited data:

* deleting overdue homework shows the full list with the new numbers,
  so the next delete can target the remaining overdue records
* homework list, edit and marks report an invalid student index first,
  and subject/ in place of s/ after a title says to use s/
* the data file accepts keys in any case, rejects a key repeated in
  another case, and refuses to load a key TutorFlow does not use,
  instead of dropping it at the next save

preferences.json still ignores unknown keys. The User Guide and
Developer Guide cover the new messages, the delete steps and full due
dates earlier in the year.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #213 from Edison-choo/211-normalize-student-search
commitResults.messageBody:
Match equivalent Unicode forms in student search

Let search find a name when an accented letter is typed in another
Unicode form, such as e followed by a combining accent for é. Each
value and the keyword are compared as typed and also after NFC
normalization, so existing partial matches, such as part of a
decomposed Hangul name, still work. The feedback keeps the keyword
as the user typed it, and the User Guide notes the new matching.

Also expand two single-line Javadoc comments to the course format.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow combining marks in student and guardian names
commitResults.messageBody:
The name validator rejects combining marks used in ordinary
non-English names and decomposed accented names.

Accept Unicode marks while retaining the existing length and
whitespace rules. Add parsing, boundary and persistence tests,
and align the guides with the supported input.

Fixes #216

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject names containing only combining marks
commitResults.messageBody:
Names made entirely of combining marks and spaces are accepted and
can render blank, allowing invisible student and guardian names.

Require at least one character other than a combining mark or space.
Retain support for Indic and decomposed accented names. Add model,
add-parser and edit-parser regression cases, and align the guides.

Validation: focused name, parser and storage tests and both
Checkstyle tasks pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify lesson invariants and Javadocs
commitResults.messageBody:
Lesson deletion assumes the selected lesson belongs to its owner, but
does not check that removal succeeds. Several class and method headers
also use a Javadoc layout outside the course convention.

Assert the removal result without putting the mutation inside assert,
and expand the affected headers and constructor documentation. Keep
normal command behavior unchanged when assertions are disabled.

Refs #214

commitResults.messageTitle: Strengthen lesson and UI regression tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The layout regression can pass without its mutation commands succeeding.
Long UI tests also mix setup and assertions, and a child-process
readiness read can wait indefinitely.

Check the resulting lesson state before geometry, extract focused UI
helpers, and bound readiness and process cleanup. Preserve the font and
width matrix, scrolling checks, and actual-overflow synchronization.
Add a blocked-lock regression for timeout cleanup.

Refs #214

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix scrolling over result panel padding
commitResults.messageBody:
The result panel's outer padding does not scroll its text because
forwarding only covers the inner ResultDisplay root.

Route gestures from the full placeholder through the existing viewport
forwarder. Preserve its guards against duplicate events, and compare
forwarded line and pixel gestures with direct viewport scrolling in
both directions while retaining the command draft and focus.

Update the UG and DG with the behavior, routing and manual test.

Refs #212, #214
